context.requirement_text: REQ-204: SSRF validation for webhook target_url. Adds pure-function Letflow.Webhooks.UrlValidator module and wires it into create/2 and dispatch_http/3. No process, no supervision, no migration.

task.description: Idiom review of REQ-204 implementation. Check: (1) OTP idiom - UrlValidator is a pure-function module with no process, appropriate for this job; (2) supervision integrity - no new supervised processes added, nothing to review; (3) scope creep - confirm no changes outside the intended scope (url_validator.ex, webhooks.ex, security-invariants.md); (4) decision-record consistency - confirm the choice to NOT add fe80::/10 (IPv6 link-local) is explicitly flagged in the design and deferred properly rather than silently omitted; (5) @spec completeness - validate/1, validate/2, and all private helpers have @spec; (6) create/2 @spec includes the new {:error, :target_url_not_allowed} return variant; (7) Bitwise usage is correct (import Bitwise vs use Bitwise).
acceptance_criteria: UrlValidator is appropriate as a plain module (not a GenServer/Agent/process)
No unintended scope creep (only url_validator.ex, webhooks.ex, security-invariants.md changed)
fe80::/10 omission is explicitly flagged (in design §7 OQ-1) not silently missed
Bitwise import is correct OTP usage

otp_idiom.notes: Letflow.Webhooks.UrlValidator is a plain module with no process of any kind — no GenServer, Agent, ETS writes, registry lookups, or spawn. Pure functions: URI.parse/1, :inet.parse_address/1, :inet.getaddrs/2, pattern matching, guards. Appropriate for pure validation work.

supervision_integrity.notes: No new supervised processes added. No use GenServer/Agent/Supervisor anywhere in url_validator.ex. Webhooks.ex supervisor topology unchanged.

scope_creep.notes: git diff main..feature/WF02-REQ204-20260831 --name-only returns exactly: url_validator.ex (new), webhooks.ex (modified), security-invariants.md (modified), req204-ssrf-validation.md (new design doc), handoff files, docs/requirements.yaml, docs/status/ (2 files). No surprise source file changes.

decision_record_consistency.notes: fe80::/10 omission is documented in design §7 OQ-1 — explicitly flagged and escalated, not silently missed. OQ-1 text: 'ELIXIR-DEV should flag this to REVIEWER at implementation time and recommend adding it — but must not silently add it as scope creep. If REVIEWER approves, the INV-9 text in §5 is updated before ELIXIR-DEV merges.' OQ-1 satisfied the check: this is fine.
decision_record_consistency.oq1_reviewer_decision: APPROVE: fe80::/10 should be added. It is the IPv6 link-local range — same attack class as 169.254.0.0/16 (already blocked). Fix is one line in blocked_ipv6?/1: 'defp blocked_ipv6?({a, _, _, _, _, _, _, _}) when a in 0xFE80..0xFEBF, do: true'. Report to ORCH as a pending finding (security-gap tag, high priority); ORCH should route to ELIXIR-DEV before merging.

spec_completeness.notes: validate/1 has @spec. validate/2 has @spec. create/2 @spec includes {:error, :target_url_not_allowed} as a variant. All public functions have @spec. OBSERVATION (not a criterion failure): dispatch_http/3 and dispatch_http/4 are private (defp) and lack @spec — inconsistent with url_validator.ex's exhaustive private-function spec coverage but acceptance criterion says 'all PUBLIC functions have @spec' and both are defp.

bitwise_usage.notes: import Bitwise is correct (not use Bitwise). Operators used: >>> (bsr/2, logical right shift) and &&& (band/2, bitwise AND) in ipv4_from_mapped_ipv6/1. Both are part of the Bitwise stdlib since Elixir 1.12. No name collision risk — &&&/2 and >>>/2 are infix aliases for band/2 and bsr/2; nothing in the existing webhooks.ex codebase uses these operators.

dispatch_delegation.notes: dispatch_http/3 delegates to dispatch_http/4 by passing &UrlValidator.default_resolver/1 as the injected dns_resolver. Idiomatic for test-injectable parameters in Elixir. do_dispatch_http/3 contains the actual :httpc.request/4 call. Indirection depth (3→4→do_dispatch) is appropriate: the extra arity carries the injectable seam needed for DNS-rebinding property tests (design §6.2 AC4).

issues_to_report_to_orch.title: UrlValidator: fe80::/10 (IPv6 link-local) not blocked
issues_to_report_to_orch.description: blocked_ipv6?/1 does not cover fe80::/10 (the IPv6 link-local range, 0xFE80..0xFEBF in the first 16-bit group). This is the IPv6 equivalent of 169.254.0.0/16 which is already blocked. An attacker with control over a webhook target_url could supply a literal [fe80::1] address to reach link-local services. Fix: add 'defp blocked_ipv6?({a, _, _, _, _, _, _, _}) when a in 0xFE80..0xFEBF, do: true' before the catch-all clause. INV-9 text should be updated to list fe80::/10 alongside fc00::/7. REVIEWER decision: APPROVE adding this before merge.

result.summary: PASS — all 7 acceptance criteria met. One pending finding for ORCH: fe80::/10 (IPv6 link-local) is missing from blocked_ipv6?/1. REVIEWER approves adding it; ORCH should route to ELIXIR-DEV before merge. Minor observation only: dispatch_http/3 and dispatch_http/4 (both private) lack @spec, inconsistent with url_validator.ex's exhaustive coverage.
